Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-10 - UNVERIFIED BLIND IMAGE READING

Exposure / process statement
- Nothing in my context proposed an identification or a reading of this text. This is a blind reading.
- Beyond the rules, the only extra step was an `ls` of the two assigned packet directories, to get the image filenames. I opened PROMPT.md and image-001..022 only. All 22 images loaded.
- The modern pencil labels written on the supports are visible in the images ("Stams, STA, Frg. 161-1r", "-2r", "-3r", "-4r", "-5r" on one side; "161-1v ... 5v" on the other). I report them as observations only.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- image-001 (overview, side "r") and image-010 (overview, side "v") each show five pieces of parchment:
  piece 1 (label 161-1): the largest leaf fragment, about 13 x 19 cm. One column of a single text block in a small, informal Gothic book hand (cursive-influenced), brown ink. The text runs for about 28-29 lines on 1r. The lower third of 1r is blank. The top edge is cut and damaged, with a notch/hole near the top centre.
  piece 2 (label 161-2): a narrow vertical strip, about 4 x 19 cm. It holds only the left-hand beginnings of lines from one column (line-starts on 2r; on 2v, the line-starts sit at the right side of the strip because the leaf is turned).
  pieces 3, 4, 5: small scraps. 3r shows a red stroke and the remains of one or two lines. 3v has red offset and a word fragment. 4r/4v and 5r/5v show red smudges or offset only; I see no legible text.
- Rubrication: red touches on capitals (letter-stroking) and red paraph strokes inside the line before new sentences ("¶ Der ..."). Some small red marks sit in the left margin of 1r. 1v has two red horizontal rules across the column (one about two-thirds down, one near the foot under a final line). 2r has a red rule under one line near the foot.
- There are no running titles, no enlarged initials beyond red-stroked capitals, and no interlinear glosses beyond occasional superscript letters and corrections.
- Marginal notes: in the left margin of 1r at about line 13 there is a short word ("gote"? / "sch"?, about three letters, ink). A small "a"/"n"-like mark appears at about line 21.
- Language (observation): vernacular German prose, with one or two Latin words in 1r about line 20. Interpretation (tentative): a continuous prose treatise on the stars/planets, the days of the week and virtues (1r), and on confession and shame (1v, upper part). I do not identify it.

SELECTED SPANS
- 1r: nearly all legible lines (1-29). Main images: image-005 (upper right), image-004 (left half), image-008 and image-009 (lower half). The tiles overlap, so I give one combined line sequence per face, with the images that show each line.
- 1v: lines 1-34. Images: image-013, image-014, image-017, image-018, image-021, image-022.
- 2r and 2v strips: line-starts only (one to three words per line).
Unread: scraps 3-5 (practically blank); the first abraded line at the top of 1r; the right-hand ends of the 1r and 1v lines that are lost at the torn top right.

Conventions: (xx) = my expansion of an abbreviation; word? = uncertain reading; [illegible] = I cannot read it; [...] = text lost at an edge, hole or crop; ¶ = red paraph or red-stroked capital at a sentence start; d' = d with superscript abbreviation (der/daz).
